The core strategy shift is to select clues that are semantically tight to the target set and explicitly distinct from the opponent/distractor lists before submitting.

New plan: I failed because my clue "reaction" was too broad and semantically linked to the distractor "checkup" (medical reaction) or potentially "spider" (allergic reaction), causing my partner to guess incorrectly. With only one target word ("allergy"), I must provide a clue that is uniquely specific to that word and completely disjoint from the distractors (riddance, sorcerer, spider, checkup, teacher) and the kill word (census).
